fixed_statement:
Let \(E\) be Polish. Let \((P_s)\) and \((P_s^n)\) be Markov semigroups on \(E\). Fix \(0<\varepsilon<t\). Assume:

1. For every \(x\in E\),
\[
P_t^n(x,\cdot)\Rightarrow P_t(x,\cdot),
\qquad
P_{t-\varepsilon}^n(x,\cdot)\Rightarrow P_{t-\varepsilon}(x,\cdot).
\]

2. For every compact \(C\subset E\), there is \(a(C)>0\) such that
\[
\operatorname{Aff}(P_\varepsilon^n(v,\cdot),P_\varepsilon^n(w,\cdot))\ge a(C)
\]
for all \(n\ge1\) and all \(v,w\in C\).

\[
P_t(x,\cdot)\not\perp P_t(y,\cdot)\qquad\forall x,y\in E.
\]
If this holds for some \(t>0\), then \((P_s)\) has at most one invariant probability measure.
fixed_proof: For arbitrary \(x,y\in E\), Lemma 6.2 gives total variation distance strictly smaller than \(1\), hence the two limiting transition probabilities are not singular. The uniqueness assertion is Lemma 6.3.
